entries.title: A cause from one of two men: each alone is bound to nothing harmless when certain of his own state

statement.note: Ibn Rajab, qāʿida 14: «فهل يلحق الحكم بكل منهما أو لا يلحق بواحد منهما شيء». The first riwāya on the two who find al-manī rests on each one's certainty: «لا يلزم واحدا منهما غسل ولا وضوء نظرا إلى أن كل واحد منهما متيقن للطهارة شاك في الحدث»; taken together, «فينظر إليهما مجتمعين في حكم يتعلق باجتماعهما».

refs.note: The two riwāyas on the shared garment; the first on each one's certainty.

refs.excerpt_ar: ينام فيه هو وغيره، وكانا من أهل الاحتلام على الصحيح من المذهب، وعنه يجب.
refs.note: al-Inṣāf: no ghusl, «على الصحيح من المذهب».

refs.excerpt_ar: إذا كان الثوب لا ينام فيه غيره ممن يحتلم. فإن كان كذلك فلا غسل على واحد
refs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā, decisively: neither owes the ghusl (and neither follows the other in prayer: the joint ruling).

conditions: a cause of obligation or prohibition from one of two, not known which
each is certain of his own prior state and doubts only the breach
the ruling is harmless (ṭahāra), not one that would cut a right (divorce, manumission)
each is taken alone, not together in one ruling
entries.rationale: Two contributions read qāʿida 14 differently. The M8 reading (attachTo) takes Ibn Rajab's farq: binding both is harmless in ṭahāra, cuts a right in divorce. It therefore binds each in the shared-garment case, which the madhhab rejects: al-Inṣāf, al-Furūʿ and Sharḥ al-Muntahā give no ghusl to either, as the ledger's graded evidence for 14.f000 records. The other reading (oneOfTwoAttaches, tanāquḍ T-15) separates the two taken together from each alone, and puts each alone on his own aṣl (Q15). The jamʿ keeps both: each alone and certain of his own state is bound to nothing harmless, which is Q15 (q14_alone_is_q15); where a right would be cut each still abstains (Aḥmad's naṣṣ); taken together the certain cause attaches. The refinement is conservative over attachTo and departs only on the harmless case, to neither.
